title: Integrative transcriptome-proteome approach reveals key hypoxia-related features involved in the neuroprotective effects of Yang Xue oral liquid on Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease.
authors: Chen, Xiang-Yang; Cheng, Ming-Rong; Tang, Chen-Chen; Xu, Chen-Qin; Zhong, Yi-Lang; Gao, Yuan; Cheng, Xue-Xiang; Chen, Jian
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过转录组-蛋白质组整合和机器学习构建缺氧基因特征，虽涉及转录因子USF1互作预测，但核心是疾病表达分析而非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，方法为常规机器学习，与TF-DNA结合机制研究关联微弱。
abstract: Introduction: This study investigates the role of hypoxia-related genes in the neuroprotective efficacy of Yang Xue oral liquid (YXKFY) in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). Methods and results: Using differential expression and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), we identified 106 and 9 hypoxia-associated genes in AD and PD, respectively, that are implicated in the transcriptomic and proteomic profiles. An artificial intelligence-driven hypoxia signature (AIDHS), comprising 17 and 3 genes for AD and PD, was developed and validated across nine independent cohorts (n = 1713), integrating 10 machine learning algorithms and 113 algorithmic combinations. Significant associations were observed between AIDHS markers and immune cells in AD and PD, including naive CD4(+) T cells, macrophages, and neutrophils. Interactions with miRNAs (hsa-miR-1, hsa-miR-124) and transcription factors (USF1) were also identified. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data highlighted distinct expression patterns of AIDHS genes in various cell types, such as high expression of TGM2 in endothelial cells, PDGFRB in endothelial and mesenchymal cells, and SYK in microglia. YXKFY treatment was shown to repair cellular damage and decrease reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels. Notably, genes with previously dysfunctional expression, including FKBPL, TGM2, PPIL1, BLVRB, and PDGFRB, exhibited significant recovery after YXKFY treatment, associated with riboflavin and lysicamine. Conclusion: The above genes are suggested to be central to hypoxia and neuroinflammation responses in AD and PD, and are potential key mediators of YXKFY's neuroprotective action.
abstract_zh: 引言：本研究探讨缺氧相关基因在养血清脑口服液（YXKFY）对阿尔茨海默病（AD）和帕金森病（PD）神经保护功效中的作用。方法与结果：通过差异表达和加权基因共表达网络分析（WGCNA），我们在AD和PD中分别鉴定出106个和9个与转录组和蛋白质组谱相关的缺氧相关基因。开发了一种人工智能驱动的缺氧特征（AIDHS），包含AD的17个基因和PD的3个基因，并在九个独立队列（n = 1713）中进行了验证，整合了10种机器学习算法和113种算法组合。在AD和PD中，观察到AIDHS标记与免疫细胞（包括初始CD4(+) T细胞、巨噬细胞和中性粒细胞）之间存在显著关联。还鉴定了与miRNA（hsa-miR-1、hsa-miR-124）和转录因子（USF1）的相互作用。单细胞RNA测序（scRNA-seq）数据突出了AIDHS基因在不同细胞类型中的独特表达模式，例如TGM2在内皮细胞中高表达，PDGFRB在内皮和间充质细胞中高表达，以及SYK在小胶质细胞中高表达。YXKFY治疗被证明能修复细胞损伤并降低活性氧（ROS）水平。值得注意的是，先前表达功能失调的基因，包括FKBPL、TGM2、PPIL1、BLVRB和PDGFRB，在YXKFY治疗后表现出显著恢复，这与核黄素和番茄碱相关。结论：上述基因被认为在AD和PD的缺氧和神经炎症反应中起核心作用，并可能是YXKFY神经保护作用的关键介导因子。
